The attack failed, and I closed the one hole the verifier left open: the verifier proved only where the sentence is NOT, and inferred where it is. I got a witness that puts it inside the named volume.

WHAT THE VERIFIER PROVED, AND I REPRODUCED. I downloaded the same scan of A Writer's Diary (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.461396, 749,875 bytes of OCR) and searched it myself. 'breaking in as usual' -1. 'meant to write about death' -1. So the sentence is genuinely absent from Leonard Woolf's 1953 selection, and the original citation to A Writer's Diary was false. The correction to the complete diary was necessary, not cosmetic.

THE WITNESS THE VERIFIER DID NOT HAVE. OpenLibrary's search-inside runs full text across Internet Archive's scanned books, including lending items whose djvu.txt is 401. I ran the phrase through it. Among the hits, three are the volume itself: 'The diary of Virginia Woolf: 1920-1924' by Virginia Woolf, 'The diary of Virginia Woolf: Vol. 2: 1920-1924' by Virginia Woolf, and 'The diary of Virginia Woolf' by Virginia Woolf, each returning the snippet 'to write about death, only life came breaking in as usual' or the full 'I meant to write about death, only life came breaking in as usual'. That is the 1920 to 1924 volume, which is Bell's volume two, hit inside its own scanned pages. The work in the source line is therefore confirmed against the edition named, not merely inferred from the absence in A Writer's Diary. Wording confirmed too, word for word, comma for comma: no ampersand, no dash, the sentence as proposed.

THE DATE, WHICH IS THE PART STILL NOT SEEN ON THE PAGE, AND WHY IT HOLDS ANYWAY. The snippets carry no date, so I tried to break 17 February 1922 from the other side and could not. In the A Writer's Diary text the February 1922 entries run Wednesday February 15th (Peacock and Scott), Thursday February 16th (Violet Dickinson, including the exchange 'What is there to live for?' 'Your friends?' 'My friends are all dead.'), Friday February 17th (the phenacetin dose and the Dial's unfavourable notice of Monday or Tuesday), Saturday February 18th. The 18th opens: 'Once more my mind is distracted from the thought of death.' Once more. That sentence is only intelligible if the day before she had already been turned aside from the thought of death, which is exactly what 'I meant to write about death, only life came breaking in as usual' says. It cannot itself be in the 18 February entry, since it would then be redundant three words in and Leonard printed that entry from its first line. It sits at the head or foot of the unabridged 17 February entry, in the part Leonard cut. Independent quotation references give 17 February 1922, and the Yale Review essay on the making of Mrs Dalloway dates it to February 1922. Three lines of evidence, one documentary and two circumstantial, all pointing to the same day, and none pointing anywhere else. I also checked the candidate I most feared, the 16 February entry about Violet Dickinson and dead friends, and it does not fit: that entry is about the difficulty of painting a face, and its close, 'All the fluid gifts have gone in; but not the bony ones', leaves no sentence hanging.

WHAT I TRIED AND COULD NOT GET. Archive.org's djvu.txt for diaryofvirginiaw0002wool_t2u1 is 401 Unauthorized, fulltext/inside.php returns the Item not available page, BookReaderSearch.php is 404, Google Books' API is quota-zero for this project, HathiTrust and Ecosia are 403, DuckDuckGo and Mojeek serve captchas to curl, and the session's WebSearch budget ran out at 200. So the printed page of the 1978 Hogarth setting was not seen and no page number is claimed. None is needed: rule 4 accepts a dated entry as the locator, and the other three diary lines in this batch are located the same way.

EVERY OTHER GATE. shipped.js: shipped [], near [], virginia woolf 0 of 3, not banned. Attribution not in dispute, and Woolf is on no trap in the misattribution list. No speaker to name: this is Woolf in her own diary, not a character. Scope: written 1922, the volume first published 1978, so before 1999, and it is not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. Publishable: death is named, nothing is described, and the sentence's whole movement is away from death and toward life, which is the right direction at six in the morning. Theme fit for Impermanence is very good and unusually gentle for the month. Source line is 131 characters, inside the 140, leads with the author's name, uses a colon and no dash, and runs work, then volume, then locator, then edition in parentheses. The parenthesis names an editor rather than a translator, which rule 5 does not forbid and which is the honest thing to name for an untranslated diary. Tag Diary is the form of the work. Quotation ends in a full stop and contains no quote marks of any kind.

ONE NOTE-LEVEL SUGGESTION, NOT A REFUTATION. The note says the sentence 'stands in the complete diary, volume two, under 17 February 1922'. Given that the page was never seen, the honest form is that the sentence stands in the complete diary volume two, which is now confirmed, and that the day is 17 February 1922 on the agreement of the reference sources and the evidence of the following entry. The work is proven; the day is very strongly indicated. Saying so costs nothing and is what the citation standard asks for.
